objective: Measure a 16-trit hierarchical block203 decoder that reduces big-integer work in the direct Qwen3.8-27B row-scale4 GEMV

candidate.numeric_contract: bit-exact ternary decode, Q8 integer dots, and FP32 multiplication of stored FP16 row-scale4 factors
candidate.hierarchy: eight exact radix-3^16 remainders, each split into 6, 5, and 5 ternary digits

controls.constdiv: the four-limb constant-divisor direct decoder with 104 big-integer limb updates per group
controls.generic_direct: the repeated unsigned-128 divmod direct decoder
controls.aligned_two_bit: the aligned two-bit row-scale4 AVX2 kernel with identical factors and arithmetic contract
controls.freeze_boundary: no authoritative generic-direct or constdiv timing result had been observed when this gate and its thresholds were frozen

static_correctness.scalar_equivalence: bit exact against both generic and constdiv decoders
static_correctness.x86_cross_object: candidate AVX2 inner symbol and scalar tail helper contain no __udivti3 references or integer divide instructions
static_correctness.interpretation: static structure and scalar equivalence motivate an empirical gate but are not a throughput result

measurement.cpu_affinity: one frozen physical core supplied by the watcher

promotion_rules: run only after the full 666-tensor row-scale reconstruction and storage gate and both earlier direct-kernel watchers are terminal
a valid threshold miss is retained as a hierarchical-decoder negative
a pass authorizes container-integration work but proves neither model quality nor token throughput
CUTE, MATH, code, MMLU-type, WikiText, and paired end-to-end throughput remain mandatory
infrastructure-invalid work is neither a zero nor a completed result
no scientific breakthrough claim can come from this isolated kernel
